newsitem.title: UK: C&W Panama deal pricey, seen lifting earnings.
newsitem.headline: C&W Panama deal pricey, seen lifting earnings.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Plc's $652 million investment in a 49 percent stake in Panama's national telecoms group should boost earnings despite its hefty price, analysts said on Wednesday.

Cable and Wireless is paying $4,150 per line for effective operational and management control of INTEL -- a bid that was over 40 percent higher than a competing one from GTE Corp and well above Panama government expectations.
Although average prices in Europe are just under $1,500 per line, Adrian Goodall, telecoms analyst at SBC Warburg, says the value is justified by higher growth rates.
Goodall compares the price with $4,500 per line for Telefonica del Peru, $3,000 for Cia Telecomunicaciones de Chile SA of Chile and around $3,400 for Brazil.
"We estimate average CAGR (compound annual growth rate) of 18 percent in EBITDA for Latin American operators," he said.
Panama is a highly developed urban economy, which C&W compares to the markets of Hong Kong and Singapore. But it has a line penetration of only 12 percent, offering significant scope for growth.
"On 1996 profitability, the deal should both enhance earnings per share (by 0.4p to 28.4p in 1997/98) and reduce the EV/EBIDTA by 0.1 to 8.2 times," Goodall said.
